mapping.assumptions: Pure state algebra only; neither statement supplies network delivery or liveness guarantees.

differences: Idempotence concerns duplication of one state; commutativity concerns ordering two states.

result.rationale: Distributivity links sequencing to join, whereas the monoid rules give sequencing associativity and the no-effect identity. These are complementary interface obligations, not duplicate statements.

mapping.carriers: The same total program-effect carrier E in the chosen effect-quantale profile.
mapping.equality: Carrier equality on effects, with the stated order/join conventions.
mapping.operations: Distributivity uses both sequencing and join; the monoid condition uses sequencing and epsilon.
mapping.assumptions: Total operations, potentially noncommutative sequencing, and no inferred concurrency or reordering guarantee.

differences: Different operation combinations and quantified equations.

result.rationale: The elimination equations cover different disjoint constructors of a sum. One specifies the inl/f branch and the other the inr/g branch, so they are separate required cases.

mapping.carriers: A tagged sum A+B and a common result carrier C.
mapping.equality: The chosen typed extensional equality on C.
mapping.operations: case(f,g,inl(a)) uses f; case(f,g,inr(b)) uses g.
mapping.assumptions: Total functions with the respective A→C and B→C types and disjoint tagged constructors.

differences: Different constructors, branch functions and input carriers.
Exchanging tags and branch names is not deletion of one required branch equation.

result.rationale: The shared frame shape explains the high text score, but freeing makes the selected address unallocated while writing stores Some(v). Both preserve other addresses and express different heap effects.

mapping.carriers: Finite partial maps from positive natural addresses to a value carrier V.
mapping.equality: Extensional heap equality with explicit None/Some observations.
mapping.operations: free removes the selected binding; write updates the selected binding to v.
mapping.assumptions: The selected address is allocated; invalid access, address reuse and lack of concurrency follow the stated snapshot profile.

differences: Different state updates at the selected address.
The common frame condition does not make deletion and update interchangeable.
